threats.name: ARTEX
threats.summary: ARTEX is an open-source, AI-driven penetration-testing framework (a Go server with a Next.js web console, default port 8787) published on GitHub in July 2026 and taken down on 8 October 2026; copies and forks still circulate. Criminal and state-aligned groups use it to automate intrusions against internet-facing systems, and the FBI warned about it on 13 November 2026. It is not a vulnerability: there is nothing to patch. Two prebuilt Docker Hub images (tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex) were reported to carry a backdoored login handler.

needs.checks: the Stackurity agent on each server looks for an ARTEX console or binary installed or running there
container images (from the agent's Docker access or a connected registry) are checked for ARTEX and for the backdoored tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex images
connected repositories are checked for a copy of ARTEX or a file that runs its images

threats.name: CyberStrikeAI
threats.summary: CyberStrikeAI is an open-source, AI-driven offensive security platform written in Go (github.com/AIPentest/CyberStrikeAI, Go module cyberstrike-ai, web console on port 8080 by default) with web shell management and a built-in command-and-control server. On 24 November 2026 Unit 42 reported campaigns, tracked from July to September 2026, in which autonomous AI agents followed web shells on vulnerable web applications, mostly on Linux web servers, then compiled public exploits on the target (Copy Fail CVE-2026-31431, CVE-2024-1086, PwnKit) to become root; the command-and-control server behind them also ran CyberStrikeAI. It is not a vulnerability: there is nothing to patch. Finding it on a server you did not put it on means the server is being used for an attack or someone installed it without the security team knowing. Patch the kernel and the web applications those agents start from.

needs.checks: the Stackurity agent on each server looks for a CyberStrikeAI server binary (by its Go build record) or a copy of its source installed there
container images (from the agent's Docker access or a connected registry) are checked for a CyberStrikeAI binary built into them, and for images named like it
connected repositories are checked for a copy of CyberStrikeAI's source (a go.mod declaring its module) or a file that runs an image named like it

threats.name: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialisation (CVE-2026-129448)
threats.summary: Apache Roller, a Java blog server deployed in Tomcat or another servlet container, deserialises data sent to its XML-RPC endpoint (/roller-services/xmlrpc) before it checks who is asking, so anyone who can reach it can run code on the server. Releases 4.0.0 to 6.1.4 are affected (CVE-2026-129448), and 6.1.5 too (CVE-2026-82384, the same flaw). It is being exploited, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 20 November 2026. Upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later. Until then, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, and restart Roller: turning XML-RPC off in Roller's administration pages is not enough.

needs.checks: the Stackurity agent on each server finds Apache Roller deployed in Tomcat or Jetty (an unpacked web application or a .war file) and reads its release from roller-version.properties
container images (from the agent's Docker access or a connected registry) are checked for Apache Roller deployed in a Tomcat or Jetty webapps directory

threats.name: nginx2root (nginx memory-corruption bugs fixed in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7)
threats.summary: nginx2root is the name researchers gave five memory-corruption bugs in nginx, disclosed on 18 November 2026. Each can crash an nginx worker, and the researchers say they can be used to run commands on the server as the nginx worker: CVE-2026-123007 (HTTP/2 flow control, nginx 1.9.5 to 1.31.8, any listener with HTTP/2 on), CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2 use-after-free, 1.19.7 to 1.31.8, HTTP/2 with proxy_pass), CVE-2026-121810 (HTTP/3 use-after-free, 1.25.0 to 1.31.8, HTTP/3 with proxy_pass), CVE-2026-123634 (resolver use-after-free, 0.6.18 to 1.31.8, a resolver with proxy_pass using variables plus mirror or SSI subrequests) and CVE-2026-113425 (mail proxy use-after-free, 0.5.33 to 1.31.8, mail proxy with auth_http). They are fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, and in nginx Plus 37.0.8.1 and 37.3.0.1; Linux distributions backport the fixes and keep the old version number, so compare the full package version with your distribution's advisory. Restart nginx after upgrading: a reload keeps the old binary running. As of 19 November there were no reports of exploitation; a public proof of concept exists for CVE-2026-123007. Until you can upgrade, turn off what you don't need: http2 off; (or remove http2 from listen on nginx older than 1.25.1), http3 off; or remove QUIC listeners, point proxy_pass at fixed upstream groups instead of variables, and keep mail listeners on trusted networks. The same researchers chained these with a separate, still unfixed Linux kernel bug in SCTP to become root from the nginx worker: on servers that don't use SCTP, add the line install sctp /bin/false to a file in /etc/modprobe.d/ (it does not unload a module that is already loaded).

needs.checks: the Stackurity agent on each server reads nginx installed from your distribution's packages or nginx.org's, and nginx built from source or installed by hand, and matches its version against the five vulnerabilities (with your distribution's backported fixes taken into account); it also flags, under Risky settings, servers where the SCTP kernel module can be loaded
container images (from the agent's Docker access or a connected registry) are checked for nginx packages with these vulnerabilities
the images your cluster's workloads run, including ingress controllers, are checked for nginx packages with these vulnerabilities
